newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Nine airmen die as Brazil air force plane crashes.
newsitem.headline: Nine airmen die as Brazil air force plane crashes.

text.p: A Brazilian air force plane crashed on Sunday in northeastern Brazil, killing all nine airmen aboard in the second fatal air force accident in two days, the military said.

Air force spokesman Maj. Francisco Lopes Neto told reporters the craft, a Brazilian-made P-95 Bandeirante, was en route to a training exercise when it went down near Caruaru, some 87 miles (140 kms) from Recife, capital of Pernambuco state.
"All those who died were air force personnel, officers and enlisted men," Lopes Neto said. "No one on the ground was hurt."

The plane, a twin-engine turboprop made by Brazilian manufacturer Embraer, left a base near the northeastern city of Salvador and was making its way up the coast to the Natal air base when it lost altitude and slammed into the ground at 5:00 p.m., he said.
"The causes of the crash are being investigated," Lopes Neto said. The plane was used by the air force as a patrol craft.

The accident came 24 hours after an air force demonstration plane lost a wing in mid-flight during an air show Saturday off the southern coast and scattered debris along a beach, killing one person and injuring five others.
